walkthroughs.body_html:
The UK has about 67 million people.

Population grows slowly, mainly due to immigration and longer lifespans.

Density averages ~280 per km2.

Most people are urban.

About 84% live in towns and cities.

The rest live in villages and the countryside.

The UK has four nations.

England is by far the largest with around 56 million.

Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland make up the rest.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.
Four-figure references are for OS maps and six-figure references are for atlases.

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a four-figure and six-figure grid reference?
options: Six-figure references are just longer versions of the same thing.
Four-figure references are for OS maps and six-figure references are for atlases.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Four-figure references identify a 1km square (eastings then northings); six-figure references pinpoint a location within that square to 100m accuracy by adding tenths.
